children: Malaysia's GDP growth could moderate to 4.5% in 4Q from 5.5% in 3Q, due to a high base and softer mining output, while domestic demand is expected to remain supportive, Kenanga economists say in a note. Private consumption may strengthen to 5.5% in 4Q from 4.3% in 3Q, supported by cash transfers and year-end spending, they reckon. Private investment is forecast to grow 7.5%, extending the capital expenditure upcycle, particularly in data center and cloud computing. Kenanga maintains its 2026 growth forecast for Malaysia at 5.3%, compared with 5.2% last year, with risks on both sides. It expects Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the policy rate by 25 bps in 1Q 2027 as a policy normalization measure rather than the start of a tightening cycle. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
